subject: CloudCart scaling playbook + rate lane proposal
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha@cloudcart.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted capacity — planning for Q2

Hi Aisha,

Quick note as we build our Q2 forecast: traffic for checkout and personalization is trending up — we expect peak token volume to rise ~2.8x month-over-month through March. We'd like to lock in a higher committed tier for hosted API to stabilize per-token costs and guaranteed throughput.

Can you share what a stepped commit (monthly ladder) would look like for 6–12 months, and how soft-throttles / burst pockets work? Also interested in any short-term burst top-ups while the commit ramps.

Cc'ing Karthik for pricing context.

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Head of Product
CloudCart
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha@cloudcart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-11T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted capacity — planning for Q2

Hi Sasha — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the growth. Short answer: yes, we can design a stepped commit + burst window that gives you predictable unit economics while preserving headroom for spikes.

High-level proposal (attached):
- Baseline commit: 25M tokens/month (3 month minimum)
- Month 4–6: automated ladder to 50M tokens/month if usage threshold hit (30% over baseline for two consecutive weeks)
- Burst pocket: +10M tokens/month at a 20% uplift to list price, usable in 24h increments
- Soft-throttle: will route lower-priority background requests to a dedicated burst lane before shedding traffic; mission-critical routes pinned to reserved capacity

I've attached: CloudCart_MAPlan_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan) and a preliminary pricing quote (pricing-quote-CC-2027-01-11.pdf).

Next steps I suggest: 1) review MA plan and mark any timing changes, 2) tell me which routes you want pinned to reserved capacity, and 3) confirm whether your procurement prefers a single monthly invoice or staged invoices per committed tier.

I'll loop in Marissa from Renewals for approval cadence once you confirm numbers.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: CloudCart — discount levers for stepped commit

Aisha / Marissa — internal note on pricing options for CloudCart: they have strong usage momentum; we can offer a graded discount that increases at each ladder step (e.g., 4% off baseline, 7% off at 50M, 12% off at 100M) if legal signs standard amendment. Need Marissa to confirm: can we approve up to 10% without involving RevOps? Also recommend a 60-day early-exit credit for their pilot phase to reduce friction.

Attachments: none in this note.

Karthik
From: Sasha Patel <sasha@cloudcart.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T14:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted capacity — planning for Q2

Thanks Aisha — the structure looks good. A couple clarifying Qs:
1) For pinning routes, we'd like checkout and personalization pinned to reserved capacity. What SLA can we expect for reserved vs. hosted lane?
2) How quickly can we provision an additional 20M burst if we see a flash sale?
3) Procurement prefers a single monthly invoice; can you reflect that in the MAPlan?

Also cc'ing Tim (CFO) who will own invoices and PO.

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha@cloudcart.com>, Tim Holt <tim.holt@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-15T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CloudCart scaling playbook + rate lane proposal

Sasha / Tim — thanks. Per your asks I've updated the MAPlan and produced a draft commit amendment that mirrors a single monthly invoice flow. Key points in the new draft (attached: commit-amendment-draft.docx):
- Reserved lanes: checkout + personalization pinned to Dedicated capacity with a 99.5% uptime target and prioritized preemption during bursts
- Rapid burst provisioning: operational SLA to enable an extra 20M tokens within 6 hours for US region, subject to both sides' change control (we'll open an ops ticket and verify capacity)
- Billing: single monthly invoice for the aggregate committed tiers + any burst consumption at the uplift rate; credit terms per usual Net 30 unless you request Net 45
- Early ladder clauses: automatic step increases will be applied after usage thresholds are met and confirmed by both parties; billing will reflect the new tier in the following invoice period

I've also added DocuSign and HubSpot links into the MAPlan (see related links). If this looks good to you, we'll move the commit amendment to legal and prepare the PO template for your finance team.

Thanks,
Aisha

Attachments: commit-amendment-draft.docx
From: Tim Holt <tim.holt@cloudcart.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CloudCart scaling playbook + rate lane proposal

Aisha — looks good. We reviewed the commit amendment with finance; please send a finalized DocuSign link and a PO template we can sign. We will target the first stepped payment on Feb 1 (baseline 25M).

Attached: CloudCart_PO_4721.pdf (blank PO for Redwood to fill in final amounts).

One operational ask: can we get a short-run checklist (ops playbook) for flash sale provisioning so our SREs know who to page? If you have an ops-runbook we can slot into our on-call rotation that would be ideal.

Tim Holt
CFO, CloudCart
